chapter: Looking back and the New York years
title: Redman and Carter as altoists with a pocket mouthpiece
summary: Smith calls Redman a technical altoist with beautiful tone who rented saxophones, and Carter the better player.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: And how do you rate, for instance, Don Redman as an alto player? How good an alto player was he?

Great. He was great. But he was a key man, what you call a key man. He played with a beautiful tone and beautiful technique. He ain't carin' about all that hot stuff. What he played was beautiful, all that technical stuff. And

Benny was the same thing. Benny was a better alto player. But both of them had the same kind of tone. They had a mouthpiece they kept in their pocket all the time. Yeah! And Don didn't even have no saxophone. He'd rent him a saxophone every time he'd get to town.

Yeah. He would find one somewhere, aronnd one of them schools. He came up one night with an old (?), but he made it sound like a Selmer -- a brand-new one. You know, they'd carry a mouthpiece in their pocket. They got a special mouthpiece that they'd carry.
